//: QA Brain -- LOCAL mode example configuration (stdio transport + SQLite + a Playwright MCP child).
cp qa-brain.config.example.json qa-brain.config.json
The gateway looks for ./qa-brain.config.json or ./qa-brain.config.yaml, or whatever
$QA_BRAIN_CONFIG / --config points at. YAML is accepted with the same keys; the hosted
counterpart of this file is deploy/qa-brain.yaml.
Every value below is also the built-in default, so a first run with NO config file behaves
exactly like this. The file exists to make the defaults visible and editable -- especially
the tool lists, which are the security boundary between an LLM and a browser.
COMMENTS: JSON has none, so these '//' keys are used instead. The schema strips unknown
keys, so they are inert -- but keep them at the top of each object, and note that a '//'
key is NOT allowed directly inside 'mcpServers', whose keys must be lowercase kebab-case
upstream ids.
Schema: packages/core/src/config-schema.ts (zod). Validate a file with `qa-brain doctor`.
String leaves support ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}; every expanded value joins the redaction
set, so a secret pulled in from the environment can never be logged.
name           reported in MCP server info; Claude Code names tools mcp__<server>__<tool>
toolsListTtlMs ttlMs advertised on tools/list (2026-07-28 CacheableResult), 5 minutes
callTimeoutMs  per proxied tool call; a navigation-heavy step can legitimately take ~30 s
maxResultChars ~20k tokens, under Claude Code's 25k-token MCP result ceiling. Over-cap
results are truncated with a `[truncated N chars]` marker, not dropped
exposeStubs    list the not-yet-implemented qa_* tools (qa_test_save, qa_heal_locator,
qa_impact_select, ...). Leave false: a listed tool that answers 'not
implemented' costs context on every turn and misleads the model
server.name: qa-brain

//: SQLite through @libsql/client (drizzle-orm/libsql). better-sqlite3 was rejected: no
prebuilt binary for Node 24 on Windows, which would force every contributor to install
Visual Studio build tools (ADR-0006).
Migrations run automatically on startup in stdio mode, so a first run against an empty
directory creates all 17 tables. `file::memory:` is valid too and is what the unit tests use.
Screenshots, snapshots and traces on the local filesystem. QA_BRAIN_HOME defaults to
./.qa-brain, which is gitignored. Hosted mode swaps this for driver 's3' against a
private SeaweedFS bucket with presigned GETs (ADR-0008).
Note this is NOT the same directory as Playwright MCP's --output-dir, which the adapter
points at ${QA_BRAIN_HOME}/pw-out.
In stdio mode pino writes to STDERR only -- stdout is the JSON-RPC channel and the
transport forbids any other byte on it, so console.log is rebound to stderr as well.
argsMode decides what action_log keeps for tool arguments:
shape    keys and types only: {"url":"string"}
redacted values after the redactor has run (local default -- useful for debugging
your own runs, and the redactor masks tokens, keys and every ${VAR} literal)
none     nothing
args_hash (sha256 of canonical JSON) is stored regardless, so the step cache and
duplicate detection work without persisting a single value. Log LINES always get the
shape, whatever this is set to. Result bodies are never stored.
Only used by `qa-brain serve --transport http`. In stdio mode the process binds no port
at all: no /healthz, no /mcp, no listener.
127.0.0.1 is deliberate. Combined with the empty allowedHosts/allowedOrigins lists it
keeps the SDK's localhostHostValidation() + localhostOriginValidation() active, which is
what makes DNS rebinding and hostile cross-origin requests fail with 403.
Fill allowedHosts/allowedOrigins only when you also change host, and then list exact
values -- they replace the localhost defaults rather than adding to them.
allowUnauthenticated is honoured ONLY on a loopback bind; the CLI refuses it otherwise
and `qa-brain doctor` flags the combination. Set QA_BRAIN_TOKEN and leave this false.
command 'playwright' is an ALIAS, not a binary on PATH. The adapter resolves it with
require.resolve('playwright/package.json') and spawns:
node <playwright pkg dir>/cli.js mcp --headless --isolated --caps=testing
--snapshot-mode=full --image-responses=omit --codegen none
--output-dir <QA_BRAIN_HOME>/pw-out --timeout-action 10000 --timeout-navigation 30000
Leaving 'args' empty gets exactly that list. Setting it replaces the whole list, so
copy the flags you want to keep. Two reasons for this shape: spawning `node` directly
sidesteps the Windows .cmd shim problem (Node >= 20 refuses to spawn .cmd without
shell: true), and pinning playwright@1.62.1 as a dependency guarantees the MCP server,
the browser revision and CI all share one version. Never npx (a registry fetch at spawn
time plus grandchildren that survive a plain kill) and never @playwright/mcp (0.0.79
depends on playwright 1.63.0-alpha, i.e. a second browser revision).
Public names are prefix + upstreamName.replace(strip, ''): browser_click -> web_click.
A collision with a native qa_* name or another upstream is a startup error, never a
silent shadow.
UPSTREAM names (browser_*), not public ones. Precedence: block beats allow beats
hidden, and qa_call_tool goes through the same lookup -- so a hidden tool is
reachable through it and a blocked tool is not reachable at all.
This is the single most security-relevant object in the file: the LLM's choices are
a function of page content, and page content is attacker-controlled.
server/discover (modern era) or ping (legacy) every 60 s, 5 s timeout, three
consecutive strikes before a restart. A degraded upstream KEEPS its names in
tools/list and answers isError with a recovery hint: a name that disappears keeps
being called from conversation history anyway.
Exponential backoff 1 s -> 30 s, five attempts. Shutdown of the child follows the
stdio transport's sequence: close stdin, 2 s, SIGTERM, 3 s, SIGKILL -- and on
Windows `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`, because Windows has neither SIGTERM nor process
groups and the node -> chromium tree would otherwise outlive the gateway.
